_readme: Source for /newsletter/. Add the newest issue at the TOP of `issues`, then run: python3 _newsletter-src/build.py. Post issues one week after they're emailed, and leave out early-access ticket links and VIP pricing (that's what subscribers get). `up_next` is the event card shown on every issue page; set it to null when there's nothing on sale. Folders starting with _ aren't published by GitHub Pages.

up_next.title: New Year's Eve at Lot Six
up_next.body: Thursday, December 31 at Lot Six on Argyle Street. Only 100 tickets, no door sales, and the first 50 come with a free 2027 Season Pass.

issues.headline: B2K drop their first album in 24 years + Silk Sonic turns 5
issues.dek: Plus T-Pain's Thr33 Ringz turns 18, and our first ever This or That.
intro: Happy Wednesday, everyone. Today is Remembrance Day, so we want to take a moment to honour everyone who has served and sacrificed. 🌺

This week we've got a brand-new album from a group we never thought we'd see back in album mode, a modern classic that turns 5, and a throwback from November 11th, 2008. We're also trying something new: This or That, where you get a say. 🤔

sections.title: Silk Sonic, “Smokin Out The Window” (2021)
body: 5 years ago this week, on November 12th, 2021, Bruno Mars and Anderson .Paak dropped An Evening with Silk Sonic.
It debuted at #2 on the Billboard 200, and “Leave the Door Open” went to #1 on the Hot 100 before winning four Grammys, including Record and Song of the Year.
sections.dyk: “Smokin Out the Window” started as a backstage joke between Bruno and Anderson, and they turned it into a hook. The funk legend Bootsy Collins named the duo and also hosts the album. That's his voice you hear on the intro.

video.label: Watch Silk Sonic, “Smokin Out The Window”

sections.title: B2K, Eclipse (2026)
body: Omarion, J-Boog, Raz-B and Lil Fizz are back with Eclipse, their first album since 2002's Pandemonium! (the album that gave you “Bump, Bump, Bump”). It's 12 tracks from a more grown-up B2K, led by the singles “Mileage” and “Lil Freak.”
sections.dyk: Bow Wow joins them on a track called “Boyfriend,” a nod to “Girlfriend,” his 2007 hit with Omarion. The album also comes off the back of their 25th anniversary tour earlier this year.

sections.title: On This Day, November 11th, 2008
body: 18 years ago today, T-Pain released Thr33 Ringz, his third album. It debuted at #4 on the Billboard 200, went to #1 on the R&B/Hip-Hop albums chart, and gave us “Can't Believe It” with Lil Wayne and “Freeze” with Chris Brown.
sections.dyk: Thr33 Ringz was nominated for Best Contemporary R&B Album at the Grammys, but it lost to Beyoncé's I Am... Sasha Fierce.

video.label: Watch T-Pain, “Can't Believe It” (ft. Lil Wayne)

sections.title: Silk Sonic vs. Silk Sonic
body: New this week! We're putting two songs head to head, and subscribers pick the winner. This week it's Silk Sonic. Which one are you running back?
Voting happens right in the email, and everyone who voted was entered to win 2 tickets to R&B at The Marquee. Results dropped in the next issue.

issues.headline: Why Whitney went funky in 1990 + Mýa's sample-free comeback
intro: Just like that, we're in the first week of November (Scorpio season). Where does the time go?! We hope the week has been treating you well.
This week we've got a fresh visual from Mýa's latest album, a Whitney Houston classic that turns 36, and an Alicia Keys album we're throwing on today just because.

sections.title: Whitney Houston, “I'm Your Baby Tonight” (1990)
body: 36 years ago this week, on November 6th, 1990, Whitney dropped I'm Your Baby Tonight. It was her third album and her most R&B-leaning one yet, with L.A. Reid and Babyface behind the boards and appearances from Luther Vandross and Stevie Wonder.
The title track hit #1 on the Hot 100 and spent two weeks at #1 on the R&B chart. The album topped the R&B albums chart too.
sections.dyk: This album was a response. After Whitney was booed (crazy!) at the 1989 Soul Train Music Awards and called “not black enough,” she went after a funkier sound on purpose. She picked L.A. Reid and Babyface because of their work on Bobby Brown's Don't Be Cruel. According to Reid, she nailed the title track in one take, in under an hour.

video.label: Watch Whitney Houston, “I'm Your Baby Tonight”

sections.title: Mýa, “Saturday Night” (2026)
body: Mýa is in full throwback mode. “Saturday Night” comes from Retrospect, her first album in eight years, a love letter to 70s and 80s funk and soul that she released on her own label, Planet 9.
The video dropped on her birthday and turns the clock back to a late-80s house party.
sections.dyk: There's not a single sample on Retrospect. Mýa skipped them on purpose, following advice she got from Prince.

sections.title: On This Day, November 4th, 2016
body: 10 years ago today, Alicia Keys released Here, her sixth album and her first in four years. 🎹
It debuted at #2 on the Billboard 200 and gave Alicia her seventh #1 on the R&B albums chart.
sections.dyk: Alicia has said she wrote around 30 songs for Here in about 10 days. Her pregnancy delayed the release, so the album sat for a while before finally coming out in 2016.

video.label: Watch Alicia Keys, “Blended Family (What You Do For Love)”

issues.headline: Dru Hill's Rush Hour classic turns 28 + NAO's surprise autumn album
issues.dek: Plus happy birthday, Frank Ocean, and the hit he wrote for someone else.
intro: Hope everybody's doing well. Is it just us, or did someone forget to tell the weather it's the end of October? ☀️ All this sun has been a treat, so hopefully you're getting outside and soaking up some fresh air while it lasts. And with Halloween weekend here, we hope you've got your costumes locked in. 🎃

One more thing... we've got something planned for later this year. 👀 A very limited capacity night that takes Bump & Grind back to its roots. That's all we'll say for now. (Update: it's New Year's Eve at Lot Six.)

sections.title: Dru Hill, “How Deep Is Your Love” (1998)
body: 28 years ago this week, on October 27th, 1998, Dru Hill dropped Enter the Dru. The album went 2x platinum, peaked at #2 on the Billboard 200 and gave us “How Deep Is Your Love,” “These Are the Times” and “Beauty.”
“How Deep Is Your Love” became the group's biggest hit, reaching #3 on the Hot 100 and holding #1 on the R&B chart for three weeks.
sections.dyk: The song was made for the Rush Hour soundtrack. Rush Hour director Brett Ratner shot the video on a rooftop in Hong Kong, and it's mixed with clips from the movie. Bonus: the album title is a nod to the Bruce Lee classic Enter the Dragon.

video.label: Watch Dru Hill, “How Deep Is Your Love”

sections.title: NAO, “Fly Away” (2026)
body: London's own NAO surprised everyone this month with Autumn, a brand-new album she announced just days before it dropped on October 16th. “Fly Away” is the standout.

Autumn is NAO's first independent album after four records with RCA. It's also the first of four seasonal albums in a series she's calling “A Soulful Suite,” and it leans into the 90s and 2000s neo-soul she grew up on.
sections.dyk: Before her solo career took off, NAO studied jazz in London and spent six years singing in an all-female a cappella group. She's also a Grammy nominee and co-wrote Ariana Grande's “Be Alright.”

sections.title: On This Day, October 28th, 1987
body: Happy birthday to Frank Ocean, born on this day in Long Beach, California. 🎈
Before he was Frank Ocean, he was writing songs for Brandy, John Legend, Beyoncé and Justin Bieber. His debut album Channel Orange (2012) went on to win the Grammy for Best Urban Contemporary Album.
sections.dyk: “Thinkin Bout You” wasn't originally meant for Frank. He wrote it as a demo for singer Bridget Kelly, who recorded her own version called “Thinking About Forever.” Frank's version leaked in 2011, and the rest is history.

video.label: Watch Frank Ocean, “Thinkin Bout You” (live on SNL)

issues.headline: “Irreplaceable” turns 20 + B2K speed things up
issues.dek: Plus the 14-year-old who dropped a debut album on this day in 1987.
intro: Hope the week is treating you well. Keeping this one short and sweet.
And yes... we may be planning something for New Year's. A VERY limited event. Keep your eyes peeled over the next few weeks. 👀 (Update: it's New Year's Eve at Lot Six, and tickets are on sale now.)

sections.title: Beyoncé, “Irreplaceable” (2006)
body: This one turned 20 this past weekend. Released October 17, 2006 off B'Day, “Irreplaceable” sat at #1 on the Hot 100 for 10 straight weeks and became the biggest single of 2007.
Twenty years later, “to the left, to the left” still gets the whole room singing.
sections.dyk: Ne-Yo wrote the lyrics, and he originally had it as a country-leaning song he was going to keep for himself. Glad he changed his mind.

sections.title: B2K, “Lil Freak” (2026)
body: Omarion, Raz-B, J-Boog and Lil Fizz are back again. After the slow burn of “Mileage” this summer, they sped things up with “Lil Freak,” a song made for the dance floor, produced by Lil Ronnie.
It's the latest taste of Eclipse, their first new album in over 20 years, which is due in November. Fair warning, this one's the explicit version. 😅

sections.title: On This Day, October 21st, 1987
body: On this day, a 14-year-old Shanice released her debut album, Discovery.
Most of us know her from “I Love Your Smile” a few years later, but this is where it started. Fourteen years old with a full album out. Wild.
